newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Overspending nudges S.African deficit above target.
newsitem.headline: Overspending nudges S.African deficit above target.

text.p: Higher than expected spending pushed South Africa's budget deficit in 1996/97 (April-March) to 5.3 percent of GDP against a targeted 5.1 percent, final budget figures released on Friday showed.

Including extraordinary receipts, represented by the sale of strategic oil reserves, the difference between expenditure and revenue was 29.66 billion rand, or 5.3 percent of the estimated GDP of 560 billion, compared to a revised estimate for the fiscal year of 28.66 billion, which represents 5.1 percent.
If extradinary receipts are excluded, the gap amounts to 31.26 billion rand, or 5.6 percent of GDP, compared to the previously estimated 5.4 percent, the finance ministry said.
The final spending total for 1996/97 amounts to 177.52 billion rand, compared to the 176.07 billion assumed in the last budget presented to parliament on March 12.
However, this expenditure overrun was partly offset by higher than expected revenues. Final revenue comes to 146.26 billion rand against the previous revised estimate of 145.81 billion.
"The higher estimate of expenditure is mainly attributable to lower than estimated unspent balances," the ministry said in a statement.
Total loan redemptions in 1996/97 amounted to 17.55 billion rand and total financing of 43.04 billion was obtained up to the end of March.

The ministry noted that the outcome of the 1996/97 could still differ from this end-year preliminary cash flow position because of surrenders of unspent funds, late requests by spending agencies and the amount of revenue in transit on March 31.
Total financing of the 1996/97 budget exceeded revised estimates by 2.02 billion rand, mainly as a result of the issuance of additional government bonds during March 1997.
Financing of 2.47 billion rand was obtained in government bonds last month while net short term loans decreased by 470.4 million rand.

The extra borrowing was undertaken in order to meet end-of-year expenditure commitments, to provide for carryover into 1997/98 and to allow for possible lags in revenue receipts as a result of a long weekend coinciding with the end of the fiscal year.
